\chapter{Communication Complexity — Derandomization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.Derandomization
\section{Overview}

This module establishes the Chernoff-plus-union-bound derandomization step at the heart
of Newman's theorem.  Starting from a public-coin protocol that $\varepsilon$-computes a
function $f : X \times Y \to \alpha$, it produces
$t = O\!\left(\log(|X|\cdot|Y|)/((c-1)^2\varepsilon^2)\right)$ explicit random seeds
that collectively cover every input: for every $(x,y)$, at most a $c\varepsilon$ fraction
of the seeds cause an incorrect output.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Hoeffding tail bound for a sum of bounded independent variables]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.prob_many_events_le}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.prob_many_events_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega', \mu)$ be a probability space, let $t \ge 1$, and let $Y_0, \dots, Y_{t-1}
: \Omega' \to \bbr$ be mutually independent, almost everywhere measurable random
variables that almost surely take values in $[0,1]$. Suppose $\E[Y_i] \le \varepsilon$
for every $i$, where $0 \le \varepsilon$, and let $c > 1$. Then
\[
\mu\!\left\{\omega \;\middle|\; c\,\varepsilon\,t \le \sum_{i=0}^{t-1}
Y_i(\omega)\right\}
  \;\le\;
  \exp\!\left(-2(c-1)^2\varepsilon^2 t\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Derandomization sample count]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p012-b002}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p005-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples}
\leanok
Given finite types $X$ and $Y$ and real parameters $\varepsilon, c$, the number of random
samples required for derandomization via Chernoff and union bound is
\[
  t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c) \;=\;
  \left\lceil
    \frac{\log(|X|\cdot|Y|)}{2\,(c-1)^2\,\varepsilon^2}
  \right\rceil_{\!+} + 1,
\]
where $\lceil\cdot\rceil_{+}$ denotes the natural-number ceiling.
\end{definition}

  {CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.integral_comp_eval, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_eq_integral_indicator_one, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.prob_many_events_le, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.rrun, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.rrun_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space and let $X$ and $Y$ be finite input sets. Let
$p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$ with
private inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
and let $\varepsilon, c \in \bbr$ with $c > 1$. Suppose $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$,
so that for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability over $\omega$ that the randomized
execution $\mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)$ differs from $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
Then, writing $t = t(X,Y,\varepsilon,c)$ for the derandomization sample count, there
exists a family $\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{t-1} \in \Omega$ of shared-randomness values
such that for every $(x,y)$,
\[
\frac{\#\{\, i \mid \mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega_i) \ne f(x,y) \,\}}{t} \;\le\;
c\,\varepsilon.
\]
\end{theorem}
